mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE rises by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) over three months indicates a strong demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where HOUST shows sustained increase over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within two months signals a contraction in the supply side of the economy, leading to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO decreases by more than 1% within two months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over a month signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it indicates inflationary pressure coupled with high borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with high interest rates
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) increases by more than 1% over a quarter and retail and food services sales (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% in the same period, it signals strong economic growth and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases > 1% and RSAFS increases > 1% in 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where GDPC1 and RSAFS both increase by more than 1% over a quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over two months, coupled with an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in the same period, signals a significant economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases > 2% and UNRATE increases > 0.5% in 2 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO decreases by more than 2% and UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% over two months.
